A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DISC research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DISC evaluations on SIGHAN, ECSpell and LEMON, including component ablations, copy-punishment experiments and decoding-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original unfine-tuned-BERT, error-type and cleaned-ECSpell experiments.

M1.justification: The decoding intervention, phonetic and glyph similarity components, and Equations (3)–(10) are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same 0.1 copy punishment. The new experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds phonetic-only and glyph-only SIGHAN15 test scenarios while retaining the three benchmark families and seven documented LEMON domains, including appendix results. The additional SIG-labeled row in v1 Table 3 disappears; its precise dataset identity is not explained.

E2.justification: v2 adds Zhou et al. (2024)'s prompt-free, training-free Baichuan2-7B comparator on LEMON, distinct from the fine-tuned Baichuan2 already reported on ECSpell. Table 5 also adds vanilla BERT with and without DISC. Existing principal comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces evaluation after removing ECSpell training examples whose correct sentences overlap the test data. Section 6 adds unfine-tuned BERT and error-isolated SIGHAN15 protocols, repairing non-target errors using a similarity threshold of 0.5. The stated basis for ECSpell seen-pair statistics also changes from the synthetic-data confusion set to training-set pairs.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether DISC helps without task-specific fine-tuning, how its effects differ between phonetic and glyph errors, and whether improvements survive ECSpell leakage removal (Tables 5, 7 and 11). Existing component ablations, sensitivity plots, case studies and copy-punishment analyses remain. The decoding-efficiency analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both Appendix A versions state that experiments are conducted once, and both Table 8 captions report decoding times averaged over three runs. v2 adds no seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for BERT, error types, cleaned ECSpell and the new LLM comparator. Cleaned ECSpell-MED reports ReLM/DISC F1 of 68.8/74.8, versus 90.2/93.9 under the retained original training setting. Table 4 revises ECSpell seen-pair percentages from 82.31/74.44/84.41 to 54.10/47.47/41.58. Table 3 removes the unexplained SIG results and adds seven-domain averages; retained individual-domain scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and encoding, classification, scoring and similarity formulas in Equations (1)–(10) match. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free, plug-and-play similarity-based decoding intervention, compatibility with existing CSC models, reduced over-correction and improved benchmark performance. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the interpretation of ECSpell performance by attributing high scores despite low seen-edit coverage to train–test leakage (Section 6 and Appendix E). It also interprets DISC's benefits for unfine-tuned BERT and explains larger gains on glyph errors. The existing language and domain limitations remain.

D1.justification: The listed code link changes from an anonymous repository to the authors' GitHub DISC repository. v2 documents bert-base-chinese initialization for the new control and the error-filtering and deduplication procedures. Existing checkpoint, fine-tuning, hardware and prompt details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhou et al. (2024) and positions its training-free, prompt-free LLM approach as a state-of-the-art comparator. The existing related-work coverage and broader novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: There are limited grammar and wording edits, added acknowledgements and localized structural changes. Decoding efficiency moves from Appendix D into Section 6, the prompt appendix becomes D, and cleaned-ECSpell experiments occupy Appendix E. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5, 7 and 11, restructures Table 3 around four displayed LEMON domains plus an overall average, and relocates existing figures and the timing table. Other LEMON domain results remain in Appendix C. Existing diagrams, sensitivity curves and the two-column presentation are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix E identifies substantial ECSpell train–test overlap and evaluates after removing duplicates, addressing an important validity gap in v1. The cleaned MED comparison still favors DISC, from 68.8 to 74.8 F1, while new controls and error analyses strengthen empirical support. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems, including the apparent precision/recall/F1 inconsistency of 66.1/71.0/70.0 in Table 11's new LAW baseline row.
